gates.reason: Inspected command/path handling and recommendation construction; the detector only classifies existing parsed artifacts and returns display data, with no authentication boundary, filesystem write, command execution, LLM egress, network sink, or client-side HTML injection sink.
The published human-time cost and causal classification are not supported by the measured field: observedMinutes is merely wall-clock time from session start to the last rediscovery-language hit.
Per-request analysis repeatedly scans all cross-session transitions and barriers for every final leave-behind state, creating avoidable multiplicative work on large ingest datasets.

findings.title: Elapsed burst span is misrepresented as causal human time cost
findings.what: observedMinutes is computed as the rounded wall-clock difference between session start and the last qualifying rediscovery-language entry. That interval can include assistant work, unrelated turns, and idle time; the nearest earlier same-project pre-signal establishes temporal association but not causation. After three bursts, the detector nevertheless states that rediscovering un-handed-off state “has cost” that many human minutes, publishes the total as estTimeReclaimedMin, and labels the claim causal.
findings.fix: Keep the value explicitly labeled as an observed elapsed burst span and classify it as accounting/observational, omitting estTimeReclaimedMin, unless an artifact directly measures active human effort and links the rediscovery to the cited missing handoff. Alternatively, add such a measured-duration field and require it for the calibrated receipt.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with three qualifying bursts containing long idle or assistant-only gaps must not emit a causal human-time claim or estTimeReclaimedMin from start-to-last-hit elapsed time; a fixture with three directly measured active-human-duration records may emit the total with provenance naming that field.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 884-914 derive the quantity solely from timestamps around language hits, lines 939-978 only associate each burst with the nearest provably earlier pre-signal, and lines 2089-2113 upgrade that association to a causal human-time cost. No direct active-human-time or causal attribution field is consumed in this file.

findings.title: Cross-session state resolution rescans global transition arrays for every final state
findings.what: For each durable session and each final leave-behind state, collectPreSignals filters the complete crossSessionTransitions array and the complete crossSessionInvalidationBarriers array. With F final states and T transitions/barriers, this performs O(F×T) predicate work and allocates new arrays/maps during every detector evaluation.
findings.fix: Build indexes once while collecting transitions, keyed by project and transition key for transitions and by project for barriers, then retrieve only the relevant buckets for each final state.
findings.acceptance: Add a detector-scale probe with increasing sessions/final states showing transition-resolution work grows approximately linearly with indexed input size; the implementation must not call full-array filter operations from inside the finalStates loop.
findings.verifyNote: The adversarial second pass re-read lines 711-750 and confirmed both global arrays are populated before resolution and are fully filtered inside the nested finalStates loop; no index or memoized lookup exists in the dispatched file.
